And under "Security" it refers to: "A Belgrade newspaper claims the town of Decani has been surrounded by the KLA the last four days. Albanian sources, however, insist that there is a bigger build-up of Serbian forces around the town preventing food-supplies from getting through. There are also reports of large numbers of police reinforcements being deployed in Glogovac (Drenica), Pec, and Srbica." Then it refers to the use of tanks and APCs noted by the ECMM. And then it refers to tanks and the ECMM. The question is this: What is your information about the truth, one side saying that KLA is surrounding Decani, the other one saying that it's the Serbian forces preventing food going through. What was your information about where the truth lay?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: I suspect somewhere in the middle, to be perfectly honest. Decani was a -- or is a patriarchal seat with a very famous monastery, and therefore an area very precious to the Serbian nation as a whole. As I've said, it's one of the key areas along the major western road and also one of the key areas to try and maintain some control over, as I said many times, a very porous and difficult border to defend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I suppose we can take this answer as an estimate -- as a guesstimate, this is the word I learned today, as you said "I suspect somewhere in the middle." There was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- the answer to where the truth would lie.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're quite right, Your Honour. There is -- in all these operations that I've come across, the media speculation is intense, in both supporting the security forces and also the media of the terrorist forces putting out their own propaganda, and one would expect that from both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And in this case you didn't have any better sources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not unless we were there and visibly saw it ourselves, and that's where we tried to make a proper judgement and report both fairly and firmly on both sides, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Re, I suppose we are close to the end of examination-in-chief, or am I completely wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] -- refer him to an ECMM one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could turn to the very beginning at tab 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: We were overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Just start your sentence once more what we are now doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turning to the very beginning of the binder, tab 3, it's under the heading: "Crosland non-DipTel proposed exhibits in chronological order." Number 3, which is 65 ter Exhibit Number 638.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All I want you to do, Colonel --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry I missed it. Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry [Indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Now we are in the first part of the binder. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's actually tab 2 and it's the 9th of April, 1998, and it's Exhibit Number 637.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is now the other part of the binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's the very beginning of the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All I want you to do is look at that document. It's an ECMM document which is provided under Rule 70, and I just want you to identify that it refers to meeting with -- a meeting between you, that's Colonel John Crosland, and ECMM officials.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wish to tender that document or have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is now 65 ter number 637, right, the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- after tab 2 in the first part of the binder. Can we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For completeness of the Limaj testimony and the exhibits -- and I appreciate the -- P92 is still under consideration, I just wish to show the Colonel the map which he used and which I think is necessary to make explicable his evidence in Limaj because it's referring to him drawing on a map. If I could just show this to the Colonel and just have him -- it's not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please. May Madam Usher show it to the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've signed it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've just been corrected. It's actually the map he drew for his June 2006 statement for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. Can you show it still to the witness. And, Colonel Crosland, may you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's Exhibit -- 65 ter Exhibit 802.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to confirm what you've drawn on that map. You've made some markings on it. What is it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND
utterances.text: This map refers to the Dukadjin area, and the various areas in blue which was where the -- there was Serb security force positions, both MUP and Vojska Jugoslavije, so -- and a big red space in the middle has got "KLA" written on it. It doesn't mean to say the KLA owned the whole area, but it was more of a KLA influence in that area. But it needs -- I mean, I think it would need further explanation to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That is enough for now. May we give it a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it receive an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P116, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Noting the time, Your Honours, I had intended to get a better explanation from the witness as to the contents of the map and what he means by "influence" versus anything else, and I had intended to ask the witness about ten documents at the beginning of the binder, not the ECMM ones. Those were my intentions, but I note the time and I note the time you've allowed me to examine the witness in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, for today we have to close. What is the position of the Defence as to these potential additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I -- I'm in some difficulties in this sense, that we have to try to make as much progress as is possible tomorrow. I can, of course, ask Mr. -- Colonel Crosland myself certain clarificatory questions. One matter that is rather important, though, is the status of the tendered 92 ter statement because Mr. Re has had the opportunity to elicit material in chief. I am assuming, in preparing for cross-examination, on the basis that the case I have to meet is the case that was led in chief and that there's no question now of me having to cross-examine on the basis of material in the 92 ter statement that wasn't elicited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you for this important question. Mr. Re, how is it for you about this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is no 92 ter statement. Is Mr. Emmerson referring to the Limaj transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The statement dated the 20 April -- in fact , 19th April. Do you remember you presented it to us this morning? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I received an e-mail from Mr. Zahar saying you had ruled against me, and I wasn't -- I hadn't tendered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You were not intending anymore to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In those circumstances, we are ad litem and I will cross-examine on the basis of the evidence elicited orally in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so far as clarification of this map is concerned, I am more than happy to deal with that myself in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Very good. And the other -- there was something else. Please, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- Mr. Emmerson is very happy to deal with it by putting a series of questions to the evidence. It's our evidence in chief. I mean, the trouble is the time. I just can't take it any further. So we're left at the disadvantage of not being able to explore with the witness what he actually meant. The cross-examination is, in my submission, not the appropriate time to explore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: There's still a re-examination chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say so, having observed Colonel Crosland in the witness box and having had the opportunity to meet him myself, I don't imagine he's the sort of person who needs any particular form of questioning to explain precisely what he means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. May we close for today, and thank you -- and please don't talk to anybody about the testimony of today or of what you will give tomorrow, but we will see you tomorrow, again at the same time at the same place. Judge Orie, our Presiding Judge, will be back tomorrow, and I wish you all a good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 20th day of April, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.10 p.m.,
